settings.title: Settings
settings.highlightModeDesc: Choose how numbers are highlighted when selected
settings.darkDesc: Pure dark theme with high contrast
settings.fastDesc: Click number, then click cell to fill. Quick and simple.
settings.cellFirstDesc: Click cell first, then click number to fill. Highlights based on selected cell.
settings.advancedDesc: Two number rows for highlighting. Select multiple numbers per colour. Cells with ALL selected numbers highlight. Click cell for action buttons.
settings.candidateModeDesc: Choose how pencil marks are managed
settings.autoDesc: Auto-calculate pencil marks based on placed numbers. Hints and error detection enabled.
settings.manualDesc: Start with blank pencil marks. Fill them in yourself. Hints and pencil mark error detection disabled.

settings.mistakeDetectionDesc: Choose when mistakes are detected and counted

settings.candidateDesc: Alert for wrong placements AND removing correct candidates

about.title: Nice Sudoku
about.tagline: A FOSS Sudoku game for all platforms by Andrew Frahn
about.description: Intended to be the easy to pick up, while also suitable for the most complex puzzles by enthusiasts.

help.title: Help
help.welcomeText: Thank you for testing Nice Sudoku.
help.author: Andrew Frahn
help.ctrlArrowKeysDesc: : Jump to the next unsolved cell in that direction
help.homeDesc: : Move to the first column of the current row
help.endDesc: : Move to the last column of the current row
help.numberKeysDesc: : Enter numbers based on play mode:
help.fastModeDesc: : Selects the number for highlighting. If a cell is selected, applies the number to that cell
help.advancedModeDesc: : Toggles the number in the primary selection. Use the two number bars for clicking (primary=blue, secondary=red)
help.ctrlNumberKeysDesc: : Toggle pencil mark candidate in the selected cell
help.spaceDesc: : If a number is selected (filter), toggle its candidate in the selected cell
help.undoButtonDesc: : Undo your last action (placements and candidate eliminations)
help.escapeDesc: : Clear all selections (selected numbers and cell)
help.f1f9Desc: : Set/change the filtered (selected) digit for highlighting
help.shiftF1f9Desc: : Set/change the filtered digit (future: toggle filter mode)
help.hDesc: : Toggle hint panel (show/hide available solving techniques)
help.requiresBackend: Requires backend connection to be available
help.enterDesc: : Set the value in the selected cell (only works when exactly one number is selected in primary)
help.deselectButtonDesc: : Click to deselect the cell and show number bars again
help.returnToGame: Return to Game screen from any other screen
help.whenEnabled: When enabled, number entry adds/removes pencil marks instead of values
help.shortcutsDisabled: All shortcuts are disabled when typing in input fields or text areas to prevent conflicts
help.hodokuConventions: Keyboard shortcuts follow HoDoKu conventions for consistency with standard Sudoku software
help.fullyPlayable: The game is fully playable using only keyboard input
help.shortcutsVary: Some shortcuts may vary slightly in behaviour between Fast, Cell First, and Advanced play modes
help.f1f9Note: F1-F9 keys: Some browsers use F-keys for developer tools (e.g., F12) or other functions. If a browser shortcut conflicts, you may need to disable the browser's shortcut or use number keys 1-9 instead for filtering
help.fastModeDetail1: Number keys select numbers for highlighting first
help.fastModeDetail2: If a cell is selected, the number is immediately applied
help.fastModeDetail3: Quick, streamlined input for faster solving
help.cellFirstDetail1: Click a cell first to select it
help.cellFirstDetail2: Then click a number to fill that cell
help.cellFirstDetail3: Highlighting is based on the selected cell's value
help.advancedDetail1: Two number bars: primary (blue) and secondary (red)
help.advancedDetail2: Toggle multiple numbers in each bar - cells must contain ALL selected numbers to highlight
help.advancedDetail3: When a cell is selected, number bars hide and action buttons appear
help.advancedDetail4: Use Deselect button to show number bars again
help.advancedDetail5: Use Set/Clr buttons to modify cells, or Enter/S for single-number selections
help.advancedDetail6: Click Fast/Cell/Adv badge in header to quickly cycle modes
help.advancedDetail7: Supports two-number highlighting for complex solving techniques
help.tip1Desc: to quickly jump between unsolved cells
help.tip2Desc: for quick number filtering and highlighting
help.tip3Desc: to access hints and learn new solving techniques
help.tip4Desc: is your universal "go back" key - use it to return to the game from any screen or modal

techniques.NAKED_SINGLE: Only one candidate fits in this cell, so place it.
techniques.NAKED_SINGLES: Only one candidate fits in this cell, so place it.
techniques.HIDDEN_SINGLE: A digit appears in only one cell of a house, forcing its placement.
techniques.HIDDEN_SINGLES: A digit appears in only one cell of a house, forcing its placement.
techniques.POINTING_CANDIDATES: A digit is locked in one line of a box, so it can be removed from that line outside the box.
techniques.POINTING_PAIRS: A digit is locked in one line of a box, so it can be removed from that line outside the box.
techniques.CLAIMING_CANDIDATES: A digit is locked in one box of a line, so it can be removed from that box outside the line.
techniques.BOX_LINE_REDUCTION: A digit is locked in one box of a line, so it can be removed from that box outside the line.
techniques.NAKED_PAIR: Two cells in a house contain exactly the same two candidates; they claim those digits.
techniques.NAKED_PAIRS: Two cells in a house contain exactly the same two candidates; they claim those digits.
techniques.LOCKED_PAIR: Two cells in a house contain exactly the same two candidates; they claim those digits.
techniques.LOCKED_PAIRS: Two cells in a house contain exactly the same two candidates; they claim those digits.
techniques.NAKED_TRIPLE: Three cells in a house contain exactly the same three candidates; they claim those digits.
techniques.LOCKED_TRIPLES: Three cells in a house contain exactly the same three candidates; they claim those digits.
techniques.NAKED_TRIPLES: Three cells in a house contain exactly the same three candidates; they claim those digits.
techniques.NAKED_QUADRUPLE: Four cells in a house contain exactly the same four candidates; they claim those digits.
techniques.LOCKED_QUADRUPLES: Four cells in a house contain exactly the same four candidates; they claim those digits.
techniques.NAKED_QUADRUPLES: Four cells in a house contain exactly the same four candidates; they claim those digits.
techniques.HIDDEN_PAIR: Two digits can only appear in two cells of a house; other candidates in those cells are removed.
techniques.HIDDEN_PAIRS: Two digits can only appear in two cells of a house; other candidates in those cells are removed.
techniques.HIDDEN_TRIPLE: Three digits can only appear in three cells of a house; other candidates in those cells are removed.
techniques.HIDDEN_TRIPLES: Three digits can only appear in three cells of a house; other candidates in those cells are removed.
techniques.HIDDEN_QUADRUPLE: Four digits can only appear in four cells of a house; other candidates in those cells are removed.
techniques.HIDDEN_QUADRUPLES: Four digits can only appear in four cells of a house; other candidates in those cells are removed.
techniques.X_WING_FISH: Rows and columns form an X-Wing so a digit can be eliminated from the covering lines.
techniques.X_WING: Rows and columns form an X-Wing so a digit can be eliminated from the covering lines.
techniques.SKYSCRAPER_FISH: Two strong links on a digit form a skyscraper, allowing eliminations in the shared columns/rows.
techniques.SKYSCRAPER: Two strong links on a digit form a skyscraper, allowing eliminations in the shared columns/rows.
techniques.TWO_STRING_KITE_FISH: A two-string kite uses 2 strong links, with a weak link in the same box, to eliminate a candidate at the intersection between the two strong links.
techniques.2_STRING_KITE: A two-string kite uses 2 strong links, with a weak link in the same box, to eliminate a candidate at the intersection between the two strong links.
techniques.2_STRING_KITE_FISH: A two-string kite uses 2 strong links, with a weak link in the same box, to eliminate a candidate at the intersection between the two strong links.
techniques.FINNED_X_WING_FISH: An X-Wing with a fin; cells seeing the fin can lose that digit.
techniques.FINNED_X_WING: An X-Wing with a fin; cells seeing the fin can lose that digit.
techniques.SASHIMI_X_WING_FISH: A sashimi X-Wing has a fin plus a missing base; cells seeing the fin can be eliminated.
techniques.SASHIMI_X_WING: A sashimi X-Wing has a fin plus a missing base; cells seeing the fin can be eliminated.
techniques.SWORDFISH_FISH: Three lines align candidates in three columns/rows, allowing eliminations (swordfish).
techniques.SWORDFISH: Three lines align candidates in three columns/rows, allowing eliminations (swordfish).
techniques.FINNED_SWORDFISH_FISH: A swordfish with a fin; cells seeing the fin lose that digit.
techniques.FINNED_SWORDFISH: A swordfish with a fin; cells seeing the fin lose that digit.
techniques.JELLYFISH_FISH: Four lines align candidates in four columns/rows, allowing eliminations (jellyfish).
techniques.JELLYFISH: Four lines align candidates in four columns/rows, allowing eliminations (jellyfish).
techniques.FINNED_JELLYFISH_FISH: A jellyfish with a fin; cells seeing the fin lose that digit.
techniques.FINNED_JELLYFISH: A jellyfish with a fin; cells seeing the fin lose that digit.
techniques.FRANKEN_X_WING_FISH: A Franken fish mixes boxes and lines to form the base/cover, enabling eliminations.
techniques.FRANKEN_X_WING: A Franken fish mixes boxes and lines to form the base/cover, enabling eliminations.
techniques.FINNED_FRANKEN_X_WING_FISH: A Franken fish with a fin; cells seeing the fin lose that digit.
techniques.FINNED_FRANKEN_X_WING: A Franken fish with a fin; cells seeing the fin lose that digit.
techniques.FINNED_MUTANT_X_WING_FISH: A mutant fish with a fin; eliminations come from cells seeing the fin.
techniques.FINNED_MUTANT_X_WING: A mutant fish with a fin; eliminations come from cells seeing the fin.
techniques.FRANKEN_SWORDFISH_FISH: A box/line swordfish variant enabling eliminations on the cover lines.
techniques.FRANKEN_SWORDFISH: A box/line swordfish variant enabling eliminations on the cover lines.
techniques.GROUPED_X_CYCLES: Grouped X-Cycles alternate strong and weak links on one digit to prove eliminations.
techniques.SIMPLE_COLOURING: Colour one digit into two sets of strong links; a contradiction colour is eliminated.
techniques.SIMPLE_COLORING: Colour one digit into two sets of strong links; a contradiction colour is eliminated.
techniques.MEDUSA_3D: 3D Medusa colours multiple digits; contradictions eliminate candidates or place values.
techniques.3D_MEDUSA: 3D Medusa colours multiple digits; contradictions eliminate candidates or place values.
techniques.THREE_D_MEDUSA: 3D Medusa colours multiple digits; contradictions eliminate candidates or place values.
techniques.UNIQUE_RECTANGLE: Prevent a deadly pattern by forcing or eliminating around a four-cell rectangle.
techniques.UNIQUE_RECTANGLES: Prevent a deadly pattern by forcing or eliminating around a four-cell rectangle.
techniques.BUG: Bivalue Universal Grave: only one candidate breaks the stalemate; place or eliminate accordingly.
techniques.BIVALUE_UNIVERSAL_GRAVE: Bivalue Universal Grave: only one candidate breaks the stalemate; place or eliminate accordingly.
techniques.Y_WING: XY-Wing (hinge + two pincers) eliminates a shared candidate seen by both pincers.
techniques.XY_WING: XY-Wing (hinge + two pincers) eliminates a shared candidate seen by both pincers.
techniques.XYZ_WING: XYZ-Wing (triad with XYZ) removes Z from cells seeing all three cells.
techniques.WXYZ_WING: WXYZ-Wing removes the shared candidate from peers of all four cells.
techniques.W_WING: W-Wing links two matching bivalue cells through a strong link, forcing eliminations.
techniques.L_3__WING: L-Wing with 3 cells links candidates to force eliminations.
techniques.L_WING: L-Wing links candidates in an L-shaped pattern to force eliminations.
techniques.EMPTY_RECTANGLE: An empty rectangle forces a conjugate pair interaction to eliminate a candidate.
techniques.EMPTY_RECTANGLES: An empty rectangle forces a conjugate pair interaction to eliminate a candidate.
techniques.X_CYCLES: X-Cycles alternate strong/weak links on one digit; contradictions remove candidates.
techniques.X_CYCLE: X-Cycles alternate strong/weak links on one digit; contradictions remove candidates.
techniques.XY_CHAIN: XY-Chains link bivalue cells; the target digit is eliminated where both ends see.
techniques.AIC: Alternating Inference Chain proves eliminations via alternating strong/weak links.
techniques.AIC_TYPE_2: Alternating Inference Chain (Type 2) proves eliminations via alternating strong/weak links.
techniques.ALTERNATING_INFERENCE_CHAINS: Alternating Inference Chain proves eliminations via alternating strong/weak links.
techniques.FORCING_CHAINS: Forcing chains explore both outcomes and keep the deduction common to all paths.
techniques.RING: A ring structure of strong and weak links forces eliminations at junction points.
techniques.ALMOST_LOCKED_SETS: Almost Locked Sets connect via restricted candidates to force eliminations.
techniques.ALS_XY: ALS-XY links two almost locked sets through a shared restricted candidate.
techniques.ALS_XZ: ALS-XZ links two almost locked sets through shared restricted candidates.
techniques.SUE_DE_COQ: Sue-de-Coq divides a box-line overlap into disjoint digit sets, forcing eliminations.
techniques.NISHIO: Nishio assumes a digit placement and prunes branches that lead to contradiction.
techniques.AIC___ALS: Alternating Inference Chain combined with Almost Locked Sets to force eliminations.
techniques.AIC_TYPE_1: Alternating Inference Chain (Type 1) uses strong/weak link alternation to prove eliminations.
techniques.XY_CHAINS__TYPE_1: XY-Chain (Type 1) links bivalue cells; the target digit is eliminated where both ends see.
techniques.ALS_CHAIN: ALS-Chain links multiple almost locked sets in sequence to force eliminations.
techniques.SPLIT_WING: Split-Wing uses a split pattern of candidates to force eliminations.
techniques.STRONG_WING__WINDMILL_: Strong-Wing (Windmill) uses a windmill pattern of strong links to eliminate candidates.
techniques.INVERTED_H_3__WING: Inverted H(3)-Wing uses an inverted H-shaped pattern with 3 cells to force eliminations.
techniques.INVERTED_M_3__WING: Inverted M(3)-Wing uses an inverted M-shaped pattern with 3 cells to force eliminations.
techniques.INVERTED_L_3__WINGS: Inverted L(3)-Wing uses an inverted L-shaped pattern with 3 cells to force eliminations.
techniques.UVWXYZ_WING: UVWXYZ-Wing (6-cell wing) removes the shared candidate from peers of all six cells.
techniques.HIDDEN_XY__TYPE_1: Hidden XY (Type 1) uses hidden bivalue cells in an XY-chain pattern to eliminate candidates.
